meta.title: AgriRot — Choose what to plant, wisely
meta.description: Simple advice to choose what to plant, season after season, based on the rain and heat in your area. You always decide.

common.disclaimer: AgriRot supports your decision; it does not replace your judgement or local agricultural expertise.

priorities.coverCropHint: Velvet bean (mucuna) and sunn hemp are cover crops: they are not harvested, they feed and protect the soil between two crops.

strategies.title: Compare rotation strategies
strategies.liveData: Live NASA data · calculated on 14/11/2026 at 11:30
strategies.footnote: The score (0–100) measures how well the strategy fits your plot and your priorities. Stability shows how well this score holds up under stress scenarios (rain −20%, +2 °C): it is not a second score.
strategies.sequenceHint: Sequence · tap a season to change the crop
strategies.seasonsTitle: Why two seasons, S1 and S2?
strategies.seasonsText: In Yaoundé it rains twice a year. S1 is the first rainy season: sowing in March, rain until June. S2 is the second: sowing in August, rain until November. The rest of the year is too dry to sow without watering, so AgriRot suggests one crop per rainy season, two per year.
strategies.remindersText: Get a message before each sowing and each harvest.
strategies.remindersNext: Next reminder: sowing {crop}, end of February {year}.
strategies.computingHint: AgriRot is combining NASA data for your area with your information. This can take a few seconds.
strategies.horizonHint: 2 seasons a year. Changing the length recomputes the plan.
strategies.plannedNote: Planned rotation: your planned crops season by season, then your usual crops (your history) for the seasons you did not plan. Without history, those seasons stay fallow.
